title: This $1500 Carbon Bike is CRAZY Good Value! (SAVA A7L Pro Bike Review)

takeaways.text: Bought from SAVA's official AliExpress store for about US$1,557 (with an US$80 coupon); it arrived in eight days with no import fees from a US warehouse.
The bike arrived with torn bar tape, a cut hood cover and a fork paint chip from a transit-damaged box; SAVA support asked him to get it repaired locally and covered the invoice.
He says the Pro differs from the cheaper A7L by using the full Shimano 105 R7120 groupset (hydraulic brakes and shifters) instead of SENSAH-mixed parts, for about US$200–300 more.
He quotes 8.9 kg for the bike; the stock 25 mm tires are its weakest point and he plans 30–32 mm tires, though SAVA lists 25C as the R08 maximum and no wider fit is shown.

It smooths road buzz without feeling sluggish, accelerates and climbs well and is stable at speed; the bars sit about 2–3 cm lower than on his Trek Domane, and the narrow bar felt less stable out of the saddle.
Minor flaws: small bubbles in the chainstay protector, two plastic bumps on the stem that had to be cut off to fit, and matte paint that shows every mark; the seatpost has an anti-slip coating.

disclosure: The presenter says he bought the bike with his own money and has no relationship with SAVA; the description carries AliExpress affiliate links.
summary: First-impressions review after roughly 500–600 km on a size-L SAVA A7L Pro with Shimano 105 R7120, including shipping damage handling and a comparison with a Trek Domane SL5.
